description.value: The study examined resting-state functional connectivity and graph-theory network organization across the C9orf72 mutation spectrum, comparing C9+ carriers with healthy controls, symptomatic bvFTD+ with ALS-only carriers, and relating hub node strength to behavioral impairment.

value: We hypothesized that functional imaging in C9+ carriers would show a hybrid pattern on a continuum of those seen in ALS and FTD reflecting the relative balance of motor and cognitive-behavioral dysfunction in each patient.

We hypothesized that C9+ with bvFTD/ALS-FTD would exhibit changes in networks associated with cognitive-behavioral function whereas C9+ FTD—ALS patients would exhibit changes in motor networks, and that network measures would correlate with clinical measures of motor or cognitive-behavioral function.

value: C9+ carriers had significantly lower global network density and lower mean connection strength than healthy controls; clustering coefficients also differed, while path length and modularity were not further explored because they are sensitive to network density.

Overall, global network measures of connectivity were reduced in C9+ carriers compared with healthy controls, with no substantial reorganization of network hubs, indicating a relatively diffuse global decline in connectivity.
